> **Supplementary Figure 6.** No single surface database recovers more than a fraction of the genome-wide accessible surfaceome the triage agent identifies. Because no hand-curated truth exists at genome scale, agreement is measured across all 19,324 protein-coding genes against the production two-stage triage verdict (yes, contextual, or no) as the reference. A database surface call agrees with an agent yes or contextual; a non-surface call agrees only with no. The databases fall hardest on contextually surface proteins, for which none has an explicit category.
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

Whole-genome analog of the 147-gene bench plot
`db_correctness_by_class`. On the bench, ground truth is hand-curated;
on the whole proteome (19,324 protein-coding genes) it doesn't exist,
so we use the **production two-tier Sonnet triage verdict as the
reference**: an NCBI first pass, with 379 genes upgraded from "no" to
"yes" or "contextual" by the PubMed second-pass rescue (`verdict_source`
= `pubmed_rescue` in the TSV). For each surface DB (under its
bench-optimized cutoff) and each ≥k-DB ensemble (k = 1..5), we ask what
fraction of genes agrees with Sonnet, split by Sonnet's verdict bucket.

Soft-credit rule: DB "yes" matches Sonnet "yes" *or* "contextual";
DB "no" matches Sonnet "no" only.

Four buckets per caller:

* **overall** — across all genes with a rated Sonnet verdict
* **Sonnet = yes** — sensitivity-like
* **Sonnet = contextual** — DB must yes-vote for a match
* **Sonnet = no** — specificity-like (dominates overall by population)

10 callers total: 5 ensembles ≥1..≥5 (grey ramp, light = permissive) +
5 individual DBs under their optimized cutoffs (sorted descending by
overall agreement). Sonnet is the reference and does not appear as a
bar — it would be 100% by construction.

Run:

```
uv run make_db_vs_sonnet_whole_proteome.py
```
